record_type_quote: In our study we aimed to conceptually replicate studies conducted by Zigler and colleagues regarding specific personality traits.

targets.title: The assessment of effectance motivation in normal and retarded children.
targets.evidence_quote: Based on descriptions available in the literature, we prepared tasks similar to those that were used to differentiate the performance of people with intellectual disability and controls in the original studies (Harter & Zigler, 1974; Yando & Zigler, 1971; Zigler & Balla, 1972).
targets.outcome_quote: The results of our study do not support the hypothesis regarding differences between people with intellectual disability and people from the general population; as such, they are not in accordance with the results of previous studies conducted by Zigler and colleagues.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors state their overall results do not support the hypothesized group differences and disagree with the earlier studies; the statement covers the three named originals. Directional means and possible sample-size limitations do not override that verdict.

reasoning: Conceptual new-sample replication of three explicitly named original experimental papers. Four effectance tasks are aggregated under Harter and Zigler. Zigler (1999, 2001) describes the theory; Zigler et al. (2002) is discussed for questionnaire validity, which is not retested. Bennett-Gates and Kreitler (1999) supplies a description of the expectancy task but is not established here as a primary finding retested, so it is not added as a target.
